summary: Added orchestrator/dev_supervisor/autonomy.py (stdlib only) with next, wait, stop-hook and main-settings, plus 89 offline tests. IMPLEMENTED and TESTED offline with synthetic registries, a fake git runner and a fake clock: eligibility (PLANNED, dependencies COMPLETED/RELEASED, owned-path overlap with ACTIVE/UNDER_REVIEW tasks ignoring shared_files), tracker steps, worker results and failures with retry eligibility, submitted-but-unmerged waves, idle reasons, wait change/timeout, Stop hook block/allow/loop-bound/fail-open/other-session, settings shape. OBSERVED once: next --json against this checkout and the real machine-local state returned 3 items (2 review_step, 1 verify_wave), 0 blocked, 0 warnings, state directory unchanged. NOT TESTED: a real Claude Code session invoking the hook, wait run as a real background command, hook run through claude --settings. Wiring main-settings into launch.py is PROPOSED (later task). Known limit: a wave merged by squash is not an ancestor of origin/main, so it can be listed as verify_wave until its remote branch is deleted. Fix round 2 (Main's live findings): review_step and start_step items are actionable only for tasks owned by --owner (default claude:repository-coordinator); other owners' steps are listed in others_waiting_review, outside the fingerprint, and never make stop-hook block. A wave is closed (never verify_wave) when all its lanes' task ids are COMPLETED/RELEASED in ACTIVE_TASKS.json (what governance wave close writes, per closeout_records) or its manifest records a closed state; ancestry is no longer the only signal.
